assumptions.load order: ~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua runs bootstrap, then default.hypr.omarchy (helpers, autostart, monitors, workspaces, bindings, gestures, envs, looknfeel, qconsole, input, windows, pop), then the current theme's hyprland.lua, then the user files hypr/{monitors,input,bindings,looknfeel,autostart}, then the toggle files and saved workspace layouts last (config/hypr/hyprland.lua:4-29; default/hypr/omarchy.lua:3-32; default/hypr/toggles.lua:11-27). A toggle therefore beats both the theme and the user's looknfeel.
assumptions.user overrides: Stock config/hypr/*.lua ship with everything commented out (config/hypr/looknfeel.lua:1-55), so the defaults below are what a fresh install runs.
assumptions.toggles: No toggle files enabled: transparent (not opaque or glassy) windows, theme corners, gaps on, animations on, no single-window aspect ratio (default/hypr/toggles.lua:4-17; bin/omarchy-hyprland-window-transparency:13-21; bin/omarchy-hyprland-corners:11-19).
assumptions.workspace mode: No saved workspace layouts, so every workspace runs Hyprland's general.layout = dwindle (default/hypr/looknfeel.lua:21; bin/omarchy-hyprland-workspace-layout-default:21-26).
assumptions.theme: Tokyo Night, the install default (install/user/theme.sh:10). It ships no hyprland.lua of its own, so default/themed/hyprland.lua.tpl renders with hyprland_active_border falling back to accent = #7aa2f7 (themes/tokyo-night/colors.toml:3; bin/omarchy-theme-set-templates:34-47, 102-123, 324-331).
assumptions.hyprland version: Config is Hyprland's Lua API (hl.config, hl.bind, hl.window_rule). Comments cite measurements on Hyprland 0.56.2 (default/hypr/qconsole.lua:176).
assumptions.bar: Top bar 26px reserved at the top of each monitor (see services.json assumptions); used only in derived geometry examples.
assumptions.units: Hyprland sizes in logical px. Animation speed is in deciseconds (1 unit = 100ms), as Omarchy's comment says (default/hypr/looknfeel.lua:76).
assumptions.key codes: code:10..19 are the digit row 1..0, code:20 is minus, code:21 is equal, code:34/35 are the bracket keys, code:201 is a vendor key (XKB evdev keycodes). mouse:272 is the left button, mouse:273 the right.

layout.layout: Every workspace tiles with Hyprland's dwindle layout by default. Gaps are 5px per window side inside (so 10px between two neighbouring windows) and 10px to the monitor edge; borders are 2px; corners are square (rounding 0); shadows and blur are off. The focused window's border is the theme accent (Tokyo Night: solid #7aa2f7; Omarchy's base gradient is rgba(33ccffee)->rgba(00ff99ee) at 45deg, used only before a theme loads); unfocused windows have rgba(595959aa). A new tiled window splits the focused window's node in two equal halves. force_split = 2 always places the new window on the right or bottom half, never by cursor side. Whether it goes side by side or stacked is Hyprland's rule: side by side if the node is wider than it is tall, otherwise stacked. preserve_split keeps a split's orientation once set, including after Super+J flips it. Worked example (derived, 1920x1080 at scale 1, 26px bar): one window's outer box (border included) is x 10, y 36, 1900 x 1034. A second window on its right gives two 945 x 1034 boxes with a 10px gutter (x 10 and x 965). A third, opened from the right-hand window (945 wide < 1034 tall, so it stacks), splits the right column into two 945 x 512 boxes, 10px apart. Floating windows draw the same 2px border; Omarchy sets no option to remove it, except per-rule border_size = 0 (pip, Hermes HUD). Borders can be grabbed for resizing with an 8px extended grab area and a resize cursor on hover. Super+L cycles the active workspace dwindle -> scrolling -> floating -> dwindle (Super+Alt+L goes back). The choice is saved per workspace. Scrolling is Hyprland's own scrolling layout, with each column 49% of the screen width. Floating is Omarchy's own mode: it floats every window, adds titlebars and a dock, and makes focus click-to-focus. The master layout is configured (new windows become master) but nothing in Omarchy selects it.

floating.layout: Windows float only by rule. The workhorse is the floating-window tag: anything tagged floats, centred, at 875x600. Tagged apps: Omarchy's own TUIs and installer terminals (org.omarchy.btop, org.omarchy.terminal, org.omarchy.bash, TUI.float), foot's org.codeberg.dnkl.foot id, the GNOME previewer and Evince, windows of class Omarchy or About, imv, mpv, every xdg-desktop-portal-gtk dialog, Sublime/OnlyOffice/Nautilus file dialogs, 1Password, Bitwarden and Inkscape file choosers. Other float rules have their own sizes: About 920x480 centred (first launch only), LocalSend 1100x700 centred, Steam 1100x700 centred, Battle.net 1280x800 centred, captive portal 900x760 centred. Picture-in-picture is 600x338, pinned, borderless, aspect-locked, 40px from the right and 4% from the top. Omacalc floats at its own size. Chromium-family browsers are forced tiled. The polkit prompt is not a window: it is a shell layer surface (namespace omarchy-polkit). Super+T toggles floating. Super+O pops a window out: float, resize to 1300x900, centre, pin to all workspaces, raise, 8px rounded corners. Press it again to undo. Super+left-drag moves a window and Super+right-drag resizes it. Hyprland places a floating window with no position rule centred on its monitor.

groups.layout: Super+G turns the focused tile into a tabbed group, or dissolves the group. While a group is focused, new windows join it (Hyprland's group:auto_group). Super+Alt+arrow moves the focused window into the group in that direction. Super+Alt+G moves it out. Tabs cycle with Super+Alt+Tab, Super+Ctrl+Left/Right or Super+Alt+scroll; Super+Alt+1..5 jumps to a tab. The groupbar is a 22px strip above the group's windows. Each tab is a gradient-filled block with monospace 12 titles: white and ultraheavy for the active tab, white at alpha 0x90 and normal weight for the rest. The fill is black at alpha 0x40 (active) or 0x20 (inactive), with square corners and a 1px indicator line 5px from the text. Tabs are 5px apart; the bar has 0px outer gap. Group borders follow the theme's active and inactive border colours. The groupbar fills and text colours are fixed, not themed.

workspaces.layout: Each monitor has its own workspaces 1-10. Hyprland numbers them globally in blocks of ten, so the first monitor has 1-10, the next 11-20, and so on. The bar labels each monitor's block 1-10. Super+1..0 goes to slot n on the focused monitor. Super+Shift+n moves the window there and follows it; Super+Shift+Alt+n moves it without following. Super+Tab and Super+scroll step through the monitor's existing workspaces. Super+Ctrl+Tab goes to the previous workspace. Workspace switches are not animated. There is no 'magic' workspace. There are three named special workspaces. scratchpad (Super+S toggles, Super+Alt+S sends the focused window) is full size with normal gaps. qconsole (Super+` toggles, Super+Shift+` sends) is a Quake console: it slides down from the top and covers the top half of the usable area. Holding one tiled window, it is a centred panel twice as wide as tall; with more windows it is full width. It has no gaps at the top or between windows, and no border. minimized holds windows minimized to the dock. Screen-share 'is sharing' indicator windows go silently to the unnamed special workspace. While any special workspace is open, the workspace behind is dimmed by 0.6. Switching to a regular workspace hides the open special workspace. The monitor rule is preferred mode, auto position, auto scale for every output, set from the display panel.

animations.layout: Animations are on. Five curves are defined: easeOutQuint (0.23,1, 0.32,1), easeInOutCubic (0.65,0.05, 0.36,1; defined but unused), linear, almostLinear (0.5,0.5, 0.75,1) and quick (0.15,0, 0.1,1). Window opens take 328ms easeOutQuint as popin from 87%. Closes take 119ms linear as popin to 87%. Moves and resizes take 303ms easeOutQuint. Opacity fades are 138ms in and 117ms out (almostLinear); other fades take 242ms (quick). The border colour change on focus takes 431ms easeOutQuint. Layers are 320ms in and 120ms out, fade style. Shell layers (bar, menus, launcher, OSD, dock, image picker, backgrounds, selection, omasnap) have no animation. Workspace switching and fadeSwitch are disabled, so switching is instant. Special workspaces slide down from the top (300ms) and slide back up (200ms), both easeOutQuint. The global fallback is 800ms on Hyprland's built-in 'default' bezier. The 'Animations Off' toggle in the menu turns off all animation, blur and shadows.

focus.layout: Focus follows the mouse: moving the pointer onto a window focuses it. Floating-mode workspaces are the exception and focus on click. Apps that ask for focus get it, except Telegram. A window focused while another is fullscreen takes over the fullscreen. Focus moves with Super+arrows and carries on to the next monitor at the screen edge. Keyboard focus changes warp the pointer to the centre of the new window, and the pointer also warps on a workspace change. Typing hides the pointer. Super+W and Super+Q both close the focused window (a polite close request, not a kill); Ctrl+Alt+Delete closes every window and returns to workspace 1. There are three fullscreen variants. Super+F is true fullscreen over the bar. Super+Alt+F is maximized: the window fills the work area and the bar stays visible. Super+Ctrl+F is 'tiled fullscreen': the app is told it is fullscreen but stays in its tile. Super+Shift+arrows swaps windows. Super+minus/equal resizes by 100px, Alt makes it 25px and Ctrl 300px; Shift switches to the vertical axis. Alt+Tab cycles windows and raises them.

appearance.layout: By default only some windows are see-through: terminals (and every TUI under org.omarchy.* or TUI.*), Omawrite, 1Password, Nautilus, LocalSend, and any window opted in with Super+Backspace. Each is at 0.985 opacity when active and 0.96 when inactive. Other windows, browsers included, are opaque. There is no blur and no dim_inactive. The Window Opacity menu has three modes. Opaque forces the opted-in windows to 1.0. Transparent is the default. Glassy turns on blur (size 4, 2 passes, brightness 0.75, vibrancy 0.35, noise 0.01), sets Nautilus to 0.75 and writes 0.65 background opacity into the terminals' own configs, so text stays crisp. Window gaps (Super+Shift+Backspace) sets gaps and borders to 0 and rounding to 0. Corners can follow the theme (0 except Solitude's 6), be sharp (0) or rounded (6, rounding_power 3). Popped windows are always rounded 8. Video apps (Moonlight, RetroArch) open fullscreen.

apps.layout: Every launch goes through uwsm-app. The terminal is foot, the first and only entry in Omarchy's xdg-terminal-exec list. It opens in the focused terminal's working directory, uses JetBrainsMono Nerd Font size 9 with 14x14 padding, and tiles with class 'foot'. The browser is Chromium, from mimeapps. Web apps are Chromium --app windows, whose classes look like chrome-<host>__<path>-Default. TUIs run in foot under the app-id org.omarchy.<command>, so they tile, except btop, which is floating-window tagged and opens at 875x600. The editor defaults to nvim as a TUI (org.omarchy.nvim, tiled). The file manager is Nautilus (org.gnome.Nautilus, tiled, transparent). The installer-presentation terminal is org.omarchy.terminal, titled 'Omarchy', floating.

notes: Hyprland-default items (not in this repo; values as documented by Hyprland's wiki for the option named in source, verify against the pinned Hyprland 0.56 if exactness matters): dwindle split rule (side by side iff w > h * split_width_multiplier), dwindle:split_width_multiplier 1.0, dwindle:default_split_ratio 1.0, dwindle:smart_split false, dwindle:use_active_for_splits true, dwindle:pseudotile false, group:auto_group true, group:insert_after_current true, bezier 'default' = (0, 0.75, 0.15, 1), animation-tree inheritance, initial floating placement centred, cursor:no_warps false, input:float_switch_override_focus 1, decoration:active_opacity / inactive_opacity 1.0, decoration:dim_inactive false.

Not in this repo: foot's default app-id 'foot' (app.terminal.class). Omarchy's rules match both 'foot' and 'org.codeberg.dnkl.foot', but only the latter is in the floating-window list (default/hypr/apps/system.lua:7). If a foot build reports org.codeberg.dnkl.foot as its default app-id, every terminal would float at 875x600; the manual's tiled terminal + browser walkthrough (manual/04-navigation.md:5-15) implies stock foot reports 'foot'.

The layout prose's worked geometry assumes Hyprland measures gaps_out to the border's outer edge and applies gaps_in on each side of each window. That is Hyprland's documented behaviour, not something this repo states.

Surprise: the task brief's 'colours from the theme' for the groupbar is only half true. Group borders follow the theme (default/themed/hyprland.lua.tpl:12-17), but groupbar fills (rgba(00000040)/rgba(00000020)) and text (white, white@0x90) are fixed in default/hypr/looknfeel.lua:52-57.

Surprise: there is no 'magic' workspace. The special workspaces are scratchpad (Super+S), qconsole (Super+`), minimized (floating mode only) and the unnamed 'special' that hides screen-share indicators.
Surprise: Omarchy 4's default terminal is foot, not Alacritty (default/xdg-terminal-exec/hyprland-xdg-terminals.list:3), and the editor binding opens nvim as a tiled TUI under org.omarchy.nvim.
Surprise: there is no 'system floats' class list for calculators beyond omacalc (no size rule), and polkit is a shell layer (omarchy-polkit), not a floating window.

Surprise: Super+L cycles three modes, and the third, floating, is Omarchy's own construction rather than a Hyprland layout. It floats windows by tag, sizes them min(1100,0.64w) x min(760,0.68h) with a 24px cascade, loads a titlebar plugin (hyprbars, 30px), turns on shadows, forces opacity 1 and switches focus to click (default/hypr/workspace-modes.lua).

Surprise: the animation timings are the pre-#16889 values cut by a fifth (default/hypr/looknfeel.lua:76-77). Workspace switches are deliberately unanimated (looknfeel.lua:92; gestures.lua:8-10), but special workspaces slide (qconsole.lua:199-200).
ALT + TAB and ALT + SHIFT + TAB are each bound twice (tiling.lua:58-61). Hyprland runs both dispatchers on one press: focus moves, then the window is raised (or the left one lowered).

The layout prose example of a third window stacking: the right-hand node is 945 wide by 1034 tall, so it is taller than wide and splits top/bottom into two 945 x 512 boxes ((1034 - 10) / 2 = 512). Derived, not a source value.
